verdict.reason: Rey Cortiço is worth a quick check for after work (16:30 start), but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide should let the sandbars work without overdoing it.

conversationalSummary.text: Rey Cortiço after work (starting around 16:30) is the best bet, but with the wind coming cross-on and the wind fit looking bad, it could turn messy quickly. I’d check the Surfline cams and the MEO Beachcam before leaving—this is one of those rare, low-consistency windows where the vibe really decides it. If the cams don’t look much better than expected, I’d skip and save the drive.

best.explanation: Rey Cortiço looks like a small north coast window for Rare window, Low confidence: 0.3-0.6 m, 27 kJ, 7 s period, lully 1/100, and wind is the main risk.  An open beach break where the sandbanks decide everything; this is best for quiet, punchy peaks when Lagide is too small; 6-9s at low tide can still work on Belgas if the sandbars are lined up, so checking exposed beaches makes sense.  Watch: Surfline consistency is lully; wind angle is poor for this spot.
